sections.h2: What does a Kentucky quitclaim deed actually transfer?
sections.html:
A quitclaim deed hands over whatever interest the signer holds in a parcel and promises nothing about how good that interest is. The McCracken County Clerk describes it as a deed that operates by way of release, passing any title or claim the grantor may have without a warranty or covenants for title. Kentucky law gives warranty deeds their own wording: KRS 382.030 turns the words with general warranty into a promise to defend the property against all persons, and KRS 382.040 limits that promise to claims made by or through the grantor.

A quitclaim deed carries neither promise. That is why it shows up between relatives, former spouses, co-heirs and people tidying up an old record, and why a buyer paying real money usually wants more than a quitclaim in the chain. Anyone who expects to resell afterward should mention the quitclaim to the closing agent early, so the title search can allow for it.

  • It conveys the grantor's interest, large or small, as it stands on the day of signing.
  • It does not create ownership the grantor never had.
  • It does not remove a mortgage, a judgment lien or an unpaid tax lien from the parcel.

sections.h2: What must a Kentucky deed contain before the county clerk will record it?
sections.html:
KRS 382.135(1) lists what every deed to real property must carry, and a quitclaim deed is a deed for this purpose. The clerk may not lodge a deed that falls short of the list, so a missing line means a rejected filing and a second trip to the courthouse.

  • The full name and the mailing address of the grantor and of the grantee.
  • A statement of the full consideration.
  • An in-care-of address where the tax bill for the transfer year can be sent.
  • A sworn, notarized certificate signed by both sides, either confirming the consideration or stating that the transfer is a gift and giving the estimated fair cash value.

Two more statutes add to the list. KRS 382.335 requires a signed statement on the deed naming the person who prepared it, along with that person's address, and it requires the grantee's mailing address. KRS 382.110 requires the deed to refer to the source of the grantor's title, by book and page when the title came from a recorded deed, or by a plain account of how and from whom the title arrived when it came by inheritance. KRS 382.130 lets a deed made in Kentucky go to record on the maker's acknowledgment before the clerk or before a notary.

sections.h2: Where is a quitclaim deed recorded, and what does recording cost?
sections.html:
Take it to the clerk's office in the county that holds the land, or the county with the larger share if a parcel straddles a line. KRS 382.110(1) sets that rule, and the 2026 General Assembly amended it effective July 15, 2026. The same date brought amendments to KRS 64.012, the fee schedule, which still lists $33 as the base charge for a deed of up to five pages.

Kentucky deed charges named in KRS 64.012 and KRS 142.050
ItemAmount
Recording and indexing a deed, up to 5 pages$33, of which $27 stays with the clerk and $6 goes to the affordable housing trust fund

Permanent records storage reimbursement$10 under KRS 64.012(3)(a)

Counties post their own totals. McCracken County's clerk publishes a $50 deed filing fee with the same $3 charge for pages past five. Phone the clerk where your parcel sits and get the all-in figure before the trip.

sections.h2: When does the Kentucky transfer tax apply to a quitclaim deed?
sections.html:
KRS 142.050 puts the tax on the grantor, and the clerk collects it before accepting the deed. When property is sold, it is figured on the full consideration, including any lien. When property is given away, or the deed shows a token price, the statute substitutes the estimated open-market value. The clerk does the arithmetic, which is why a deed that understates the price draws questions.

Subsection (7) lists the exempt transfers. Those most likely to involve a quitclaim deed:

  • Parent to child, or grandparent to grandchild, for a token price only.
  • One spouse to the other, or between former spouses in a divorce.
  • A deed that only confirms or fixes an earlier recorded deed.
  • A transfer whose sole purpose is to secure or release a debt.
  • Partition, foreclosure, or a voluntary surrender in lieu of foreclosure.
  • A trustee to a successor trustee, and certain moves into a trust whose only beneficiary is the grantor.

An exemption does not waive the filing rules. A gift deed from mother to daughter still needs the notarized fair cash value certificate under KRS 382.135 even though no tax is owed.

sections.h2: What if the grantor inherited the property?
sections.html:
A deed from someone who took title by descent has an extra step. Under KRS 382.120 the grantor, any heir at law, or two Kentucky residents with personal knowledge must hand the clerk an affidavit before the deed is filed. The affidavit names the person who died, gives the date of death, says whether that person was married, states where they lived, confirms they died without a will, and lists each heir with age, address, relationship and share.

The clerk records the affidavit and indexes it under the ancestor as grantor and each heir as grantee, charging the same fees as a deed. KRS 382.135(4) adds a duty for estates that pass by will or intestacy: before closing the estate, the personal representative files an affidavit in each county where the land lies, listing who receives each parcel and its estimated value. Heirs who sign quitclaim deeds to one another to consolidate a family house should confirm both affidavits are on file, since the clerk will not take the deed first.

sections.h2: What are the penalties for a false statement on a deed?
sections.html:
KRS 382.990 attaches criminal penalties to the paperwork. A person who willfully and fraudulently gives a false statement of the full actual consideration, or of the full estimated value, under KRS 382.135 commits a Class D felony. A person who knowingly swears to a false statement in the descent affidavit under KRS 382.120 commits a Class A misdemeanor and is liable to anyone injured by its use.

The practical lesson is to write the true figure. If a family member is paying a token amount for a house worth far more, say so on the deed and let the clerk compute the tax on market value or apply the parent and child exemption. Understating the price to save a few dollars of transfer tax creates a recorded document that can be challenged later, and a later buyer's title company will read it.

sections.h2: Does a quitclaim deed help when you plan to sell the house?
sections.html:
It can move the title into the right names so a sale can close, and it can also cause delay. A quitclaim deed leaves every lien and tax debt in place. KRS 382.070 also warns that a seller who leaves part of the price unpaid has no lien against creditors and purchasers unless the deed states what remains unpaid.

Owners who inherited a Kentucky house, fell behind on payments or hold a property with repair problems often ask whether a quitclaim to a relative will simplify things. Usually the better first step is a payoff request to the lender and the county for any unpaid tax, then a plain conversation with a closing attorney. If you want a direct cash sale of a Kentucky house as it stands, a quitclaim deed signed beforehand does not change what the buyer's title company must clear.

faqs.q: Do I need a lawyer to record a Kentucky quitclaim deed?
faqs.a: No statute makes you hire one, but KRS 382.335 requires the deed to show the name and address of the person who prepared it, signed by that person. Many people have an attorney or a title company draft the document so the consideration certificate, source of title and legal description are right on the first filing.

faqs.q: Is a notary required on a quitclaim deed in Kentucky?
faqs.a: Yes. The grantor's signature must be acknowledged, and KRS 382.135 requires the consideration or gift certificate to be sworn and notarized by both sides. County clerk offices can notarize for a fee set in KRS 64.012, so ask the clerk before you sign anywhere else.

faqs.q: What will recording a Kentucky quitclaim deed set me back?
faqs.a: State law sets $33 for up to five pages and $3 per extra page, and KRS 64.012 also allows a $10 records reimbursement. Transfer tax is fifty cents per $500 of value unless an exemption fits. McCracken County's clerk posts a $50 deed fee, so confirm the figure with the clerk who will record yours.

faqs.q: Can I quitclaim my house to my child and avoid transfer tax?
faqs.a: A transfer between parent and child for only a token price is exempt under KRS 142.050(7)(l). The deed still needs the sworn certificate that calls it a gift and states the estimated fair cash value.

faqs.q: Which office records a Kentucky quitclaim deed?
faqs.a: The county clerk where the property, or most of it, sits. KRS 382.110 sets that rule, and a deed recorded in the wrong county does not give the notice that protects the grantee against later purchasers and creditors.
